verdicts.why: I looked for an enforced bound and there is none: line 87's `contentLength < Integer.MAX_VALUE` is a cast-safety test, and the `new byte[(int)contentLength]` at line 88 runs BEFORE `in.readFully(buffer)` at line 89, so the TruncatedInputStream wrappers (lines 147, 242) cap the read but cannot cap the allocation; unlike readShortstr (line 68, bounded to 255 by readUnsignedByte) nothing bounds this path, reachable from the wire via readLongstr (103) and readFieldValue cases 'S'/'x' (162, 211). Only the words 'or server' in the impact are wrong (this is a client-side class), which does not touch the defect.

The cited cycle is exactly what the file contains: readFieldValue case 'F' (line 181) calls readTable, whose loop calls readFieldValue (line 150), and case 'A' (line 184) calls readArray, whose loop calls readFieldValue (line 245); no depth counter or parameter is threaded through any of these signatures (139, 158, 237), and the only early exit, `tableLength == 0` at line 143, is avoided simply by declaring a non-zero nested length.

Every factual element checks out: lines 86-88 read a 32-bit wire length via unsignedExtend and allocate on it, the guard permits 2147483646, and the allocation genuinely precedes any availability check because readFully is line 89 — nothing in the file (nor the TruncatedInputStream wrapping at 147/242, which only truncates reads) rejects the length before the array is requested.

The core is correct and irrefutable from this file (lines 86-88 allocate byte[] from an unsigned wire length guarded only by a cast test), though two of its three 'trigger' cites are factually wrong: lines 147 and 241 construct TruncatedInputStreams and allocate nothing proportional to the declared table/array length — only line 103 (readLongstr) and the uncited case 'x' at line 211 actually reach readBytes.

I verified every line reference (readFieldValue 158-221, 'F' at 180-181, 'A' at 183-184, the readTable loop at 150, the readArray loop at 245) and the mutual recursion is real with no depth parameter; I also tried to refute it on input economics and could not — a nested array costs only 5 wire bytes per level ('A' plus a 4-byte length), so tens of thousands of levels fit in a modest frame.

Same code as W02/W05 and it says what the claim says: readFieldValue (158-221) reaches itself through readTable (181 -> 150) and readArray (184 -> 245) with no depth limit anywhere in the file; the only overstatement is 'crashing the consumer application' — a StackOverflowError here kills the frame-handling thread and the connection, and whether the host application dies cannot be decided from this file.
